study.question: Does the aligned-membership advantage of g1-r0087 mean-only training survive when only the first scorer Dice retains its population-mean input derivative, while the second uses detached moments at identical native forward values/state and capacity?
study.hypothesis: The first scorer layer may suffice to transmit useful task-membership assignment through population-mean gradient coupling; second-layer mean coupling may be unnecessary. Local evidence motivates this because both-layer mean-only favors aligned membership while both-layer detached and variance-only do not. This is a provisional layer-sufficiency hypothesis inside the current best-model lineage, not evidence that masks add information or improve the unchanged incumbent.

inherited_components: Full incumbent item/action-aware embedding tables, target-match summaries, temporal blocks, folded five-to-seven-row support, population multiplicities, uniform click and auxiliary readouts, per-task adapters/towers and product context interaction.

All four true-label BCEs, collected context surrogate transfer including occupied-cycle source-bit nuisance-line transform, auxiliary gradient ownership and independently registered auxiliary normalization state.
The g1-r0087 explicit _PrimaryPopulationJacobian helper verbatim: mean_only=r*(g-mean(g)); detached=r*g; native primary BatchNorm forward/state/eval and FP32 moment recomputation.

Counts replacement keeps actual per-block union counts/support emptiness but replaces both membership/complement contents with the valid block mean. Permutation rotates all supplied task bits by the same valid-rank map in each temporal block, then forms the inherited auxiliary union.
study.proposed_difference: Add plain architecture metadata primary_mean_layers=first_only. Select self.local_activation[1] (Dice64) to retain the inherited mean_only VJP; self.local_activation[3] (Dice32) uses inherited detached VJP. No new modules, buffers, RNG, moment recomputation, forward rows or state updates. Three standalone sources differ only in membership_use=full/counts/permuted. The both setting is an unexecuted source bridge to g1-r0087; second_only is an unexecuted complementary factorial setting, not a reported experiment.
predictions: Predeclared direction: first_mean_only full click AUC exceeds both first_mean_only counts and first_mean_only permutation; report both differences even if only one favors full.

If first-layer mean coupling suffices in this implementation, the aligned-versus-control ordering from both-layer mean-only survives first-only, whereas the historical detached-moments triad lacked that ordering. No minimum effect size or significance is promised.

At fixed identical parameters and buffers, new first_only versus both modes have equal training forward probabilities and running-state updates and identical evaluation behavior; only scorer input cotangents differ. Evaluation predictions with uniform readout should be membership-invariant at fixed state within BF16 tolerance.

All three variants retain32192421 learned parameters,31793216 embedding and399205 dense, pending host counts. Mean/variance reductions are still executed in the inherited helper for all modes; total train/inference runtime should stay near the observed455-467s full-unit range, subject to host measurement.
falsifiers: Full not exceeding either counts or permutation weakens first-layer sufficiency in this implementation; full exceeding only one leaves event-assignment attribution unresolved.

Failure to maintain the favorable membership ordering after removing second-layer mean correction leaves second-layer dependence or joint-layer interaction plausible. It does not establish either without second_only and a full factorial.

A static/numerical bridge failure, different native forward/state behavior at fixed checkpoint, changed module initialization, parameter count, mask/padding exposure or auxiliary gradient ownership invalidates this contrast rather than counting as scientific counterevidence.
Even a positive first-only contrast that remains below the unchanged incumbent does not support a better deployable model. A smaller favorable gap without independent repetition remains preliminary.

First-only vs both changes optimization of second affine-layer inputs and potentially upstream parameter gradients; an apparent effect may arise from conditioning or regularization rather than useful aligned event assignment.

The incomplete first/second-layer factorial cannot distinguish first-only sufficiency from compensating interactions with inherited nonlinear gradient transfer. No monotonic or additive assumption is made.
Per-block feedback counts, zero-row support, compression precision and inherited benchmark offline visibility may dominate small AUC differences; production point-in-time validity is unestablished.
